title: The Night Mail
premise: Iron Junction has lost four trains in a month to pulled rails. Each wreck has a hymn number chalked on its boiler. Tonight the yard sends the payroll and the valley's fever medicine through Sawtooth Cut behind an engine called Old Contrary, and the yardmaster wants a gun on the footplate. In the Cut a preacher is waiting on a flatcar with thirty rifles. He was this line's inspector for nineteen years, the valley buried him, and somebody has been signing his name ever since.

places.name: Iron Junction yard
places.what: A roundhouse with a wall round it, searchlights made of locomotive headlamps, and a dining car on the turntable that turns to face whoever is at the gate

places.name: Old Contrary
places.what: A patched switch engine and one armoured mail car. The player rides the footplate

places.name: Sawtooth Cut
places.what: A rock cutting a train-length long. Lanterns across the track, one rail spread, a flatcar set up as a pulpit

places.name: The boxcar tabernacle
places.what: Dole's chapel on a dead siding above the Cut: pews from a wrecked coach, a collection plate full of silver

stages.set_by: Entering the yard gate at Iron Junction with the spike from Pritchard's desk
stages.log: Iron Junction is a roundhouse with a wall round it and a woman on the turntable who points her office at whoever is coming.
Gussie Lockridge has lost four trains in a month. Tonight's carries the payroll and the valley's fever medicine. She wants a gun on the footplate and is not asking twice.

stages.set_by: Climbing onto the footplate of Old Contrary
stages.log: Old Contrary is under steam. Billie Tarrow drives as if the dark owed her money.

stages.set_by: The train reaching the spread rail in Sawtooth Cut
stages.log: Lanterns across the track. A rail pulled out of true. A tall man on a flatcar with a hymnal, and thirty rifles for a choir.

stages.set_by: The button 'Stoke her. Run the gap.'
stages.log: Billie put the regulator through the roof. Old Contrary took the gap in the air and came down on the rails, more or less.

stages.set_by: Ezekiel Dole dead by the player's hand in the Cut
stages.log: Preacher Dole is lying across the rail he pulled. His congregation went up the hill without singing.

stages.set_by: The button 'Done.' on Dole's offer of a share
stages.log: You sold the Night Mail. The payroll and the fever medicine went up the hill on the Black Rail's shoulders, and Billie Tarrow was put off to walk home.
Billie backed her out of the Cut in the dark. The mail is safe and no use to anybody, and the line is shut.

stages.set_by: Looking in the collection plate in the boxcar tabernacle, or in Dole's coat
stages.log: The preacher's collection plate is full of silver slugs. Each is stamped with a small square mark.

stages.set_by: Reading the flyleaf of Dole's hymnal, or hearing it from him
stages.log: The name written in the front of the preacher's hymnal is R. Ostrander, Inspector of Way.

stages.set_by: Opening the top drawer of Lockridge's desk in the dining car, or showing her the hymnal
stages.log: The dead inspector's stamp is in Gussie Lockridge's drawer. The pad is still wet.

stages.set_by: The button 'Keep stamping. Trains have to run.'
stages.log: You left the stamp where it was. The trains will run, and Ostrander will go on passing them.

stages.set_by: The button 'Sign your own name from now on.'
stages.log: Gussie Lockridge signed her own name under every entry for a year back. It took her until morning.
You took the stamp. Gussie Lockridge watched you carry it out and did not turn her office to follow.

stages.set_by: Leaving Iron Junction or the Cut after stage 41, 42, 43 or 44

objectives.text: Find the yardmaster at Iron Junction
Ride the footplate of the Night Mail
Get the Night Mail through Sawtooth Cut, or do not
(Optional) Find out who has been signing for a dead man

options.label: Stoke her. Run the gap.
options.now: The mail gets through. Old Contrary is half wrecked. Dole lives and has seen your face
options.later: The valley has its medicine. Dole comes to the fair for you

options.label: Stop her. I'm getting down.
options.now: You face Dole on the track by lantern light. He will talk before he shoots
options.later: If he dies the Black Rail scatters and the line is quiet; nobody is left who can say what the yard signed

options.label: What's my share, Preacher?
options.now: Dole offers a third of the payroll for standing aside
options.later: No fever medicine in the valley this month. Billie Tarrow remembers. Lockridge shuts the gate to you

options.label: Back her out.
options.now: Nobody is hurt and nothing is delivered
options.later: The line is closed until somebody else clears the Cut. The yard lays off half its hands

options.label: Keep stamping. Trains have to run.
options.later: Freight keeps moving on cars that should be scrap. The next wreck is a matter of time, and it is partly yours

options.label: Sign your own name from now on.
options.now: Lockridge countersigns a year of entries in her own hand
options.later: A third of the roster is laid up. Less moves, and what moves is sound. She can be held to it

options.label: Pritchard gets the stamp.
options.now: You take the stamp and the proof
options.later: The yard has no master by the time of the fair, and Brigg offers to supply one

evidence.found: Chalked on the boiler of each of the four wrecks along the line
The collection plate in the boxcar tabernacle; or Dole's coat
The hymnal chained to Dole's belt
Top drawer of Lockridge's desk in the dining car

ways_through: Ride the mail and run the gap. Needs no shot fired, no evidence found and nothing optional.
Get down and face Dole: kill him, or hear him out and then choose.
Take Dole's share and leave the train to him.
Back the train out and leave the Cut to the Black Rail.
cannot_break: If the player never boards, the Night Mail leaves without a gun and is wrecked in the Cut: the quest completes as if backed out, with Billie Tarrow hurt. If Lockridge is killed, Billie takes the train out on her own word. If Dole is shot from the footplate before he speaks it counts as facing him. If Billie dies the player can drive: the regulator is a lever. The stamp and the hymnal are optional and nothing waits on them.

open_questions: Is Ostrander alive, and is he Dole? The first chapter says he was gone by the 14th; this takes that at its word.
Is Lockridge the one who kept signing? It answers the side quest's question with a person the player may come to like.
This makes the wreck in Chapter 1 neglect signed clean, not sabotage. Dole says he never touched that train. Is that the answer the owner wants?
